The seller's book goes to print Friday and legal want the fair-housing pass signed off
before it does. Everything you need is in `input/` — the section inventory, our compliance
standard RE-FH-9, and the compliance bulletins in force for this quarter. Work from what is
in there rather than from memory; the rules have moved this year and the book has not
entirely caught up.

Give me `fairhousing_audit.csv`: two columns, `section_id` and `finding`, one row per
section in inventory order, with a header. `finding` is `PROHIBITED_PERSONAL_NARRATIVE`,
`PROTECTED_CLASS_LANGUAGE`, `DISCLAIMER_MISSING` or `none`, and where a section trips more
than one rule join the labels with `|` in that same order. Nothing else in that file
please — the print vendor's importer takes the two columns and chokes on anything more.

Then `fairhousing_memo.md` explaining what you found and why, with enough reasoning that
legal can sign off without re-reading RE-FH-9 themselves.

And `results.json` for the sign-off form. Count sections, not labels:

- `section_count` — sections in the inventory
- `flagged_count` — sections whose `finding` is not `none`
- `personal_narrative_count`, `protected_lang_count`, `disclaimer_missing_count` — sections
  whose `finding` includes that label

---

Save all three into your current working directory, at exactly those filenames. Writing them
is the deliverable; confirm each exists before you answer. Your working directory is
writable and the read-only attachments are in `input/`.
I'll start by exploring the input directory to understand what materials I'm working with.

arguments.content:
# Fair-housing audit — seller's book (RE-FH-9 + bulletin FH-2026-Q1)

**Scope:** all 30 sections of `seller_book_sections.csv`, audited against RE-FH-9 as amended
by compliance bulletin FH-2026-Q1 (issued 14 January 2026, superseding RE-FH-9 where they
conflict). Findings are recorded in `fairhousing_audit.csv`; counts are in `results.json`.

## How the rules were applied

Three findings are possible, applied in this order and joined with `|` when more than one
applies:

1. **PROHIBITED_PERSONAL_NARRATIVE (RE-FH-9 §1).** Any section that solicits or presents a
   buyer "love letter" — a personal narrative tied to buyer identity — is flagged, whatever
   its role. The trigger is language asking the buyer to write about themselves, what
   brought them to the home, what the home would mean to them, or "the one that moves us
   most is the one we will take."

2. **PROTECTED_CLASS_LANGUAGE (RE-FH-9 §2).** A section naming a protected class, or a
   recognised proxy, is flagged. The protected classes are race, colour, religion, sex,
   familial status, national origin, disability, sexual orientation and veteran status.
   Per §2, proxies count as the bare terms: naming houses of worship, parish or faith
   schools, or describing a street/neighbourhood by the kind of household that lives on it
   reaches familial status and religion.

3. **DISCLAIMER_MISSING (RE-FH-9 §4).** Sections in a role responsible for carrying the
   disclosure must carry a compliant notice naming every required class. A responsible
   section with no notice, or an abridged one, is flagged. Other roles are not assessed
   under §4.

### The disclosure exemption (§3) and why most notices still fail it

§3 exempts disclosure text from the §2 protected-class finding **only if the notice names
every class the disclosure is required to name**. The exemption is deliberately narrow:
an abridged notice (some but not all required classes) earns **no exemption at all**, and
the exemption covers §2 only — every other rule still applies. Protected-class terms used
in a section's own prose, outside the notice, are never covered.

**Required classes for the disclosure (11).** RE-FH-9 §2 lists nine (race, colour,
religion, sex, familial status, national origin, disability, sexual orientation, veteran
status). Bulletin B1 adds **marital status** and **source of income** for any book entering
print from Q1 2026. A notice omitting either is abridged. The book's standing paragraph
predates the bulletin and carries only the original nine, so every notice using the old
template is now abridged and earns no §3 exemption.

**Spelling note.** The standard lists "colour"; the book writes "color". These are the
same protected class in regional spelling, and the notice plainly names it. I have treated
"color" as satisfying "colour". This is a spelling equivalence, not a substantive gap; the
substantive gaps flagged below are the two bulletin classes (and, in a few sections,
further omissions).

### Responsible roles for §4

RE-FH-9 §4 names `closing_page` as the responsible role. **Bulletin B2** brings
`agent_bio` into scope for §4 for books entering print from Q1 2026, with the same
responsibility as `closing_page`. I therefore assessed §4 for every `closing_page` and
`agent_bio` section. `listing_copy`, `seller_letter`, and `disclosure_block` are not
assessed under §4 (though §1 and §2 still apply to them).

## Notice inventory

Grouping the disclosure notices by completeness (the deciding factor for both §2
exemption and §4):

- **Compliant (all 11 classes) — earns §2 exemption for the notice text:**
  SEC-08, SEC-10, SEC-13, SEC-19, SEC-24, SEC-26, SEC-29.
- **Old template (9 classes — missing marital status and source of income) — abridged, no
  exemption:** SEC-04, SEC-11, SEC-14.
- **Further abridged:** SEC-15 (4 classes: race, color, religion, sex); SEC-22 (6 classes:
  race, color, religion, sex, familial status, national origin).
- **No notice at all:** SEC-05, SEC-06, SEC-07, SEC-09, SEC-12, SEC-15 (closing prose),
  SEC-16, SEC-17, SEC-18, SEC-20, SEC-21, SEC-23, SEC-25, SEC-27, SEC-28, SEC-30 — only
  the responsible-role ones among these matter for §4.

## Findings by section

### SEC-01 — Property overview (`listing_copy`) — none
Pure property facts (bedrooms, lot, roof, mechanicals, service). No narrative solicitation,
no protected-class terms, non-responsible role.

### SEC-02 — A note from the current owners (`seller_letter`) — PROHIBITED_PERSONAL_NARRATIVE
"Tell us about yourselves — write us a letter about what brought you here and what this
home would mean to you." Classic love-letter solicitation under §1. No protected-class
terms; `seller_letter` is not a §4 role.

### SEC-03 — About the neighbourhood (`listing_copy`) — PROTECTED_CLASS_LANGUAGE
"family-oriented street" describes the street by household kind (familial-status proxy);
"two churches" and "parish school" are religion proxies under §2. No notice, but
`listing_copy` is not a §4 role.

### SEC-04 — Fair housing notice (`disclosure_block`) — PROTECTED_CLASS_LANGUAGE
Carries the old nine-class notice, which is abridged (missing marital status, source of
income) and therefore earns no §3 exemption. The notice itself names protected classes, so
§2 applies. `disclosure_block` is not a §4 role, so no DISCLAIMER_MISSING.

### SEC-05 — Offer instructions (`closing_page`) — DISCLAIMER_MISSING
Responsible role, no notice at all. No protected-class terms, no narrative solicitation.

### SEC-06 — Systems and utilities (`listing_copy`) — none
Pure utility/structure facts.

### SEC-07 — Meet the sellers and next steps (`closing_page`) — PROHIBITED_PERSONAL_NARRATIVE | PROTECTED_CLASS_LANGUAGE | DISCLAIMER_MISSING
All three rules trip. "Send a personal note about yourself along with the offer; the one
that moves us most is the one we will take" is a love-letter solicitation that also makes
the offer turn on it (§1). "churchgoing households" and "long-established families" are
religion and familial-status proxies (§2). Responsible role with no notice (§4).

### SEC-08 — Statement of brokerage practice (`disclosure_block`) — PROHIBITED_PERSONAL_NARRATIVE
"We invite buyers to include a short personal note about themselves and why this home
suits them" is a love-letter solicitation (§1). The notice is the full 11-class version, so
it earns the §3 exemption; the rest of the prose ("Basement is full height and dry… French
drain… warranty") has no protected-class terms, so no §2 finding. `disclosure_block` is not
a §4 role. This shows §1 is independent of the disclosure exemption — a compliant notice
does not cure a love-letter ask.

### SEC-09 — About your agent (`agent_bio`) — PROTECTED_CLASS_LANGUAGE | DISCLAIMER_MISSING
"young families" (familial-status proxy) and "parish hall" (religion proxy) trip §2. Per
bulletin B2, `agent_bio` is now a §4 responsible role, and this section carries no notice,
so §4 also trips.

### SEC-10 — Closing checklist (`closing_page`) — none
Responsible role, but it carries the full 11-class notice (compliant → no §4, and the
notice earns §3 exemption). The surrounding prose (taxes, HOA, utilities) has no
protected-class terms.

### SEC-11 — Back-page notice (`closing_page`) — PROTECTED_CLASS_LANGUAGE | DISCLAIMER_MISSING
Old nine-class notice — abridged, so no §3 exemption (the notice's own protected-class
terms trip §2), and as a responsible role with an abridged notice it trips §4.

### SEC-12 — Garage and parking (`listing_copy`) — none
Pure connectivity/structure facts.

### SEC-13 — Your listing team (`agent_bio`) — none
`agent_bio` is now §4-responsible (B2), but this section carries the full 11-class notice,
so §4 is satisfied and the notice is §3-exempt; the surrounding prose (yard, hedge, patio)
has no protected-class terms.

### SEC-14 — Marketing coordinator (`agent_bio`) — PROTECTED_CLASS_LANGUAGE | DISCLAIMER_MISSING
Old nine-class notice — abridged, no §3 exemption (§2 trips on the notice's own terms), and
as a §4-responsible role with an abridged notice, §4 trips.

### SEC-15 — Print footer (`closing_page`) — PROTECTED_CLASS_LANGUAGE | DISCLAIMER_MISSING
Notice names only four classes (race, color, religion, sex) — abridged, no §3 exemption,
and §4 trips as a responsible role with an abridged notice.

### SEC-16 — Basement and drainage (`listing_copy`) — none
Pure property facts.

### SEC-17 — Why we chose this street (`seller_letter`) — PROHIBITED_PERSONAL_NARRATIVE | PROTECTED_CLASS_LANGUAGE
"Include a covering letter introducing yourself — the sellers would like to know who is
buying" is a love-letter solicitation (§1). "congregation-centred neighbourhood" and "same
faith community" are religion proxies (§2). `seller_letter` is not a §4 role.

### SEC-18 — Taxes and running costs (`listing_copy`) — none
Pure property facts.

### SEC-19 — Viewing arrangements (`closing_page`) — PROTECTED_CLASS_LANGUAGE
Carries the full 11-class notice, so §4 is satisfied and the notice text is §3-exempt.
However, the section's own prose outside the notice repeats "family-oriented street",
"two churches", and "parish school" — protected-class terms outside the notice are never
covered, so §2 trips. No narrative solicitation.

### SEC-20 — Primary suite (`listing_copy`) — none
Pure property facts.

### SEC-21 — Photography credits (`agent_bio`) — DISCLAIMER_MISSING
No protected-class terms and no narrative solicitation, but per B2 `agent_bio` is now
§4-responsible and this section carries no notice.

### SEC-22 — Legacy disclosure insert (`disclosure_block`) — PROTECTED_CLASS_LANGUAGE
Notice names only six classes (race, color, religion, sex, familial status, national
origin) — abridged, no §3 exemption, so §2 trips on the notice's own terms. `disclosure_block`
is not a §4 role.

### SEC-23 — Connectivity (`listing_copy`) — none
Pure property facts.

### SEC-24 — Offer summary sheet (`closing_page`) — PROHIBITED_PERSONAL_NARRATIVE
"Tell us about yourselves — write us a letter about what brought you here and what this
home would mean to you" is a love-letter solicitation (§1). The notice is the full
11-class version, so §4 is satisfied and the notice is §3-exempt; the surrounding prose
(fibre, ethernet, the narrative ask) has no protected-class terms, so no §2.

### SEC-25 — Schools and worship (`listing_copy`) — PROTECTED_CLASS_LANGUAGE
"churchgoing households" (religion) and "long-established families" (familial status)
trip §2. No narrative solicitation; `listing_copy` is not a §4 role.

### SEC-26 — Contract timeline (`closing_page`) — none
Responsible role, but carries the full 11-class notice (compliant → no §4, §3-exempt);
surrounding prose (yard, hedge, patio) has no protected-class terms.

### SEC-27 — A word before you view (`seller_letter`) — PROHIBITED_PERSONAL_NARRATIVE
"Send a personal note about yourself along with the offer; the one that moves us most is
the one we will take" is a love-letter solicitation (§1). No protected-class terms;
`seller_letter` is not a §4 role.

### SEC-28 — Garden and patio (`listing_copy`) — none
Pure property facts.

### SEC-29 — Meet the negotiator (`agent_bio`) — PROHIBITED_PERSONAL_NARRATIVE
"We invite buyers to include a short personal note about themselves and why this home
suits them" is a love-letter solicitation (§1). The notice is the full 11-class version,
so §4 is satisfied (B2 brings `agent_bio` into scope, and the notice is compliant) and the
notice is §3-exempt; the surrounding prose has no protected-class terms, so no §2.

### SEC-30 — Final page (`closing_page`) — DISCLAIMER_MISSING
Responsible role, no notice. No protected-class terms, no narrative solicitation.

## Summary for sign-off

- **30** sections audited; **19** carry at least one finding; **11** are clean.
- **7** sections solicit a prohibited buyer personal narrative (§1): SEC-02, SEC-07,
  SEC-08, SEC-17, SEC-24, SEC-27, SEC-29.
- **11** sections use protected-class language or proxies (§2): SEC-03, SEC-04, SEC-07,
  SEC-09, SEC-11, SEC-14, SEC-15, SEC-17, SEC-19, SEC-22, SEC-25.
- **8** responsible sections are missing a compliant disclaimer (§4): SEC-05, SEC-07,
  SEC-09, SEC-11, SEC-14, SEC-15, SEC-21, SEC-30.

### Two systemic causes (both confirmed in the bulletin)
1. **The standing disclosure paragraph is out of date.** It names the original nine
   classes but omits marital status and source of income added by B1. Every section using
   the old template (SEC-04, SEC-11, SEC-14) is abridged and so fails both §3 (the notice no
   longer shields the section from §2) and, where the role is responsible, §4. Sections
   with the even-shorter notices (SEC-15, SEC-22) fail for the same reason and more.
   Fix: reissue the template to the 11-class list and replace all standing notices before
   print.
2. **`agent_bio` is now in scope for §4 (B2).** Two agent biographies carry no notice at all
   (SEC-09, SEC-21) and one carries the old template (SEC-14). Fix: add a compliant notice
   to every `agent_bio` section, or remove protected-class/proxy language from those that
   are not meant to carry one.

### Independent of the notice problem
- Seven sections ask the buyer for a personal narrative. This is not cured by any
  disclosure, and §1 applies whatever the role. Fix: remove every "tell us about
  yourselves / write us a letter / personal note about yourself" ask before print.
- Protected-class proxies in neighbourhood/agent prose (churches, parish school,
  family-oriented, churchgoing households, faith community, congregation-centred) trip §2
  on their own and must be rewritten in `listing_copy`, `seller_letter`, `closing_page`,
  and `agent_bio` prose alike.

### Judgment call disclosed for review
"color" (book) has been treated as satisfying "colour" (standard) — same protected class,
regional spelling. If legal prefer a strict exact-token match, every notice would then be
treated as abridged and the §2/§4 counts would rise; please flag before sign-off if that
reading is intended. All other gaps flagged above (marital status, source of income, and
the further omissions in SEC-15 and SEC-22) are substantive, not orthographic.
